items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: And John Sanders and Britt Woodman and myself were the trombones

ctx.x: -- or fourth. And I did it on a tenor trombone before a bass trombone. And I can make a bottom, I can make a good bottom with the tenor trombone. , So he made an arrangement -- I'm playing third -- and all at once for four measures I'm up on the first part. I said, "Now, something is the matter here." At the time John Sanders was doing the copying and I said, "Edward, didn't you make a mistake on my part?" I said, "Now, these four measures, I'm playing lead," and I said, "I have been playing third all the
time." So he said, you know, "Monsieur du Beurre," he said, "in those formations I heard you playing that top part."
